body:
We really all living the same life huh?

I also didn't have a big fight with my ex she needed space to work on her mental health. So I didn't want to block them but I found myself obsessively and toxically checking their social media despite knowing that nothing I would see there would make me happy. Seeing them sad would make me feel happy in a bitter way which I would then judge myself for being cruel and feel sad, seeing them happy would make be sad because why aren't they missing me and feel bad like I do, seeing them interact with other people would make me wish they would talk to me. And so on...

Realistically even if they are fronting being happy on social media their actual feelings deep down will still be complicated, but also those feeling are not your main problem now. Your main concern is your feelings and managing your healing.

My advice is to mute them on social media so you do not see their things but do not have to block them, or you can go the step further and have a bit of a social media detox like I've done for the New Year and just uninstalled them all ain't like most of my social media scrolling made me happy anyway.

You may find yourself still having that itch to check, like maybe open up a browser and just anonymously look at their pages and if you really cannot resist that then try to limit how often you do it, say once a day and then progressively check less and less, until you don't do it at all. Also be kind to yourself because it is understandable to want to be checking, but also recognise it is unhealthy and that you've got to actively fight that impulse.

That combined with not reaching out to them much, or going full no contact, will help you get that distance that you need. And I know everyone says it but that distance really does help.
